cards.h: Energy is the heart of India’s climate bargain
cards.b:
India must grow its economy, give reliable power, cut imports and shrink emissions together. UPSC asks about solar, wind, green hydrogen, nuclear and storage.

Use dated numbers.

The core tension is that energy demand must grow for development, while emissions must fall. Renewable sources help with both, yet their output varies, so storage and grid upgrades matter. Energy security is another driver, as India imports most of its crude oil. Mention all five choices in answers: solar, wind, hydro, nuclear and green hydrogen.

India reached 50 percent non-fossil installed capacity in mid-2025 (about 485 GW total at the time), five years before the 2030 target. Solar crossed 100 GW in early 2025 and has kept rising (as of 2026, check MNRE).

Coal still gives roughly 70 percent of the electricity generated, because solar and wind run only part of the day.

Capacity is not the same as generation. Solar plants run at a capacity utilisation of roughly 20 to 25 percent, while coal plants run far higher, so a large renewable capacity gives a smaller share of electricity. Rajasthan and Gujarat lead in solar, and Tamil Nadu and Gujarat in wind. Grid integration and storage are the bottleneck.

The Glasgow goal is 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, with solar as the largest part, then wind, hydro and nuclear. The earlier goal of 100 GW solar by 2022 was missed.

At COP28, over 100 countries backed a pledge to triple renewable capacity by 2030. India did not sign the pledge text, saying it prefers its own targets and wants equity in burden sharing.

• PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024): rooftop solar for 1 crore homes.
  • PM-KUSUM (2019): solar pumps and feeders for farmers.
  • PLI scheme and ALMM for domestic solar modules.
  • Solar parks and the One Sun One World One Grid idea.

The rooftop scheme gives subsidy support so that households can generate their own power and sell the surplus to the grid. PM-KUSUM has three components: stand-alone solar pumps, grid-connected pumps and solarising feeders. The ALMM list names approved solar module makers to support domestic manufacturing. India and France launched the International Solar Alliance in 2015, and the One Sun One World One Grid idea links regional grids.

Launched in January 2023 with about ₹19,744 crore. Aim: 5 million tonnes a year of green hydrogen by 2030. Green hydrogen is made by splitting water with renewable power. It is for steel, fertiliser, refineries and shipping.

Challenges: high cost, electrolyser supply and storage. The SIGHT scheme supports electrolyser and hydrogen output.

Grey hydrogen comes from natural gas, and blue is grey with carbon capture. Green is the cleanest. Fertiliser and refining already use hydrogen, so the first demand exists. Pilots include hydrogen buses and trains, and hubs have been planned at ports such as Kandla, Paradip and Tuticorin.

Nuclear gives under 3 percent now. Budget 2025–26 announced a Nuclear Energy Mission with ₹20,000 crore for small modular reactors and a goal of 100 GW by 2047, with a role for private firms.

Hydropower and pumped storage give balancing. Battery storage is supported by viability gap funding. The grid needs more transmission.

Intermittency needs storage. Land is scarce. Solar equipment relies on imports, mostly from China. Critical minerals (lithium, cobalt, rare earths) are needed, and India launched the National Critical Mineral Mission in 2025.

Coal states such as Jharkhand and Odisha depend on mining jobs, so a just transition is vital.

India’s power demand is growing fast, and the government continues adding coal capacity for reliability while expanding renewables. Critics worry about stranded assets and health costs. Supporters stress energy security and affordability.

Another debate: large solar parks versus rooftop and community systems.

Coal provides baseload power and many jobs and state revenues, while its use adds to emissions and local air pollution. Renewable energy can be built faster and is now cheaper per unit, but needs storage to supply at night. Decentralised rooftop systems cut transmission losses and give households a stake. A balanced answer shows both views and then proposes a phased, just transition.

PM E-DRIVE (2024) supports electric vehicles after FAME II. Ethanol blending reached 20 percent in 2025, ahead of schedule. Energy efficiency is guided by the Energy Conservation Act 2001 and BEE star labels.

Viksit Bharat 2047 and Net Zero 2070 frame the long path.

E20 blending draws on sugarcane and grain, so critics link it to water use and food prices. Electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers and buses are the main focus of PM E-DRIVE. The BEE star label rates appliances such as air conditioners. The Energy Conservation Act 2001 created the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, and a 2022 amendment added a basis for carbon markets.

Mains-style: “Discuss the challenges in India’s transition to renewable energy and suggest solutions.” Structure: progress (50 percent non-fossil capacity); barriers (intermittency, grid, import dependence, financing, land, coal jobs); solutions (storage, green hydrogen, domestic manufacturing, nuclear, just transition).

Prelims tip: NGHM 2023, target 5 MMT. PM-KUSUM 2019. PM Surya Ghar 2024. ISA 2015.

Extra points: the transition is a just transition issue for coal states such as Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. Dependence on imported solar cells and critical minerals is a risk, and a PLI scheme for solar modules supports local manufacturing. Use examples: Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan, Pavagada in Karnataka, and Cochin airport as a solar-powered airport.

quiz.q: India reached 50 percent non-fossil installed capacity in:
quiz.w: Five years ahead of the target.

quiz.q: The National Green Hydrogen Mission targets how much by 2030?

quiz.w: PM Surya Ghar is for homes.

quiz.q: Which scheme supports rooftop solar for 1 crore homes?
o: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana

quiz.q: PM E-DRIVE replaced which earlier scheme?
Which share of electricity generation does coal give (approx.)?
quiz.w: Even though capacity share is lower.

quiz.q: The National Critical Mineral Mission was launched in:
quiz.w: For lithium, cobalt and similar minerals.
